preamble: Deaffrication of the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] to the voiceless palatal stop [c] is a regional realization rather than a widespread change. It is best documented in Canary Islands and Cuban Spanish, where traditional 'ch adherente' is articulated as a palatal stop with little or no fricative release, and may voice to [ɟ] between vowels.

examples.note: 'Boy'. The traditional Canarian 'ch adherente' is a palatal stop; intervocalic voicing gives [ɟ].
